_comment: Tracks real, popularity-weighted OSS Terraform/OpenTofu estates run through the five-stage crossing pipeline (cold deploy -> migrate -> test plan -> test apply -> drift and reconverge), same spirit as cohort-acceptance.json but for real-world estates rather than estate-gen's synthetic cohorts. A stage is 'pass', 'fail', or 'not_run' - not_run means the estate's script does not yet exercise that stage, which is itself a gap worth closing, not a silent pass. Updated by the orchestrator from each crossing's own verified run, not by an agent editing this file directly - the same discipline live/cohort-acceptance.json uses, so N concurrent crossings never fight over one JSON file's sort order.

estates.source: hand-written reference project: the plainest getting-started shape (VPC/subnet/SG/IGW/EC2)
estates.notes: Verified end-to-end 2026-08-17/18. Predates the drift-and-reconverge stage being added to the pipeline shape; needs a follow-up pass to add it, same as every other pre-existing corpus-* script.

Landed f6a9f899d0 (2026-08-18), which also fixed a real generalizing bug on the way: live-import's Ratify loop skipped every resource inside a module block (regressed behind closed issue #59's child-module admission, which named five other root-only walkers but never live-import). module.lambda_function.{aws_lambda_function,aws_iam_role,aws_cloudwatch_log_group} now stamp correctly - this affects every real module usage, not just this estate, since virtually all published Terraform modules nest their resources under a module block. test_plan blocked on a separate, still-open gap: two resource blocks (aws_lambda_function_url, aws_lambda_function_recursion_config) use count = var.enable_x ? 1 : 0 with the var false/unset, so stock OpenTofu creates zero instances of either, but choudoufu's type-admission check runs per declared block rather than per resolved instance and refuses the plan outright. A local_file resource is also refused (outside the live-markers subset). Recommended next slot: a static count-is-zero evaluator feeding type admission - likely high-leverage, since count-gated optional-feature resources are an extremely common module idiom, not specific to this one.
